title: Naked Maps representing Domain Entities
pattern: Using raw key-value maps (`HashMap`, `BTreeMap`) to represent structured domain entities.
why_bad: It completely eliminates compile-time type checking. Keys are checked at runtime, making simple spelling mistakes (e.g., `"firstname"` vs. `"first_name"`) compile successfully but fail at runtime. It also incurs unnecessary heap allocations and hash-computation overhead.
detection: Core business variables structured as `HashMap<String, String>` or `HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>` where the keys represent entity fields.
counterexample: A generic indexing system, an arbitrary configuration store, or a cache layer mapping dynamic runtime user values.
fix:
Define a formal, typed struct representing the entity.
```rust
struct UserProfile {
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
}
```
source: *Domain Modeling made Functional* by Scott Wlaschin (p. 110).
